AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2's pool-wide verdict, copied not re-derived. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation IS construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect (TerritorialPower 1 on itself, Byrdonis.cs:34-38) is applied from `__init__` (byrdonis.py:26-28). The game applies it from MonsterModel.AfterAddedToRoom (MonsterModel.cs:313-316 is a no-op base, so the override is the whole effect), awaited by CombatManager.AfterCreatureAdded inside StartCombatInternal, i.e. after every creature is on the board and before Hook.BeforeCombatStart. Same observable today on all three clauses SHARED-FINDINGS establishes by execution: (a) listener set -- the only ported listeners on the reachable hooks (relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38, relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53, relics/vambrace.py:26-40, relics/paels_legion.py:36-43) all gate on the player and a monster's starting power/block is self-applied with no card; (b) HP-roll inversion -- of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp and only inside revive() (powers.py:2067), never at apply time; (c) roll ordering -- all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-ops (monster_probes.py roll-order).  Rule 7: the four relic files and sts2_rl/powers.py named above are NOT hashed by this record (powers.py is hashed only where this record cites it with line numbers).

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: A MachineMonster port, so the graph is comparable node for node. Byrdonis.cs:40-51 builds PECK_MOVE and SWOOP_MOVE, sets PECK.FollowUpState = SWOOP and SWOOP.FollowUpState = PECK, and -- the easy thing to get backwards -- passes moveState2 (SWOOP) as the INITIAL state, not the first-declared PECK. The port matches: swoop.follow_up = peck, peck.follow_up = swoop, MonsterMoveStateMachine([swoop, peck], swoop). No RandomBranchState anywhere, so no AddBranch integer to misread. guards.what: Range-bound convention on the initial-HP roll: Rng.NextInt(min, max) is max-EXCLUSIVE (Rng.cs:101-109) where Python's random.randint(a, b) INCLUDES b
guards.rationale: Checked as a convention, not just as constants. The GAME's range is [MinInitialHp, MaxInitialHp] INCLUSIVE, because Creature.SetUniqueMonsterHpValue compensates for the exclusive bound explicitly: `int num = Monster.MaxInitialHp + 1` (Creature.cs:378) feeds BOTH `Enumerable.Range(minInitialHp, num - minInitialHp)` (Creature.cs:379) and the fallback `rng.NextInt(minInitialHp, num)` (Creature.cs:383). The sim's parity port matches on both arms: `candidates = [v for v in range(lo, hi + 1) ...]` picked with `niche.next_int_range(0, len(candidates))`, fallback `niche.next_int_range(lo, hi + 1)` (combat.py:423-442, `_roll_parity_hp`), and `next_int_range` is itself max-exclusive (rng.py:182-186) -- so the two `+ 1`s land exactly where C# puts them. This unit has a real 4-wide range, so a top-end off-by-one would be silently observable as HP 84 never occurring. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py hprange`, 400 seeded combats per unit): declared [81,84], observed [81,84], and the observed set is exactly the full inclusive range, so the top endpoint 84 does occur. All 15 units of this batch pass. NOTE the legacy (non-parity) path is also right by a different route: Monster.__init__'s `rng.randint(self.min_hp, self.max_hp)` (monsters/base.py:236) is inclusive on both ends, matching the game's inclusive range, and in parity mode it is overwritten before anything reads it. Rule 7: Creature.cs, Rng.cs, sts2_rl/combat.py and sts2_rl/rng.py are hashed in extra_sources.
